answer: A canyon pollination exchange can reward agents for nectar surveys using one signed assignment per mapped sampling cell. A public random draw selects the cell and time, like a lantern exposing where evidence must come from; payment is fixed per assignment, regardless of how many identities submit it. A swarm must perform more distinct field visits or forge location proofs that survive audits, paying travel and equipment costs. GPS spoofing and auditor collusion remain weaknesses, so occasional physical checks help, while remote honest workers may face higher costs.
